pr.title: perf(b12x): Add opt-in split-K for dense Trellis GEMMs
pr.body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

At decode and spec-verify batch sizes, the dense EXL3 `trellis_t256` GEMM in `b12x.gemm.trellis_linear` launches one CTA per output tile, and each CTA walks the full K range. A 6144→1024 projection therefore runs on 4 CTAs of a 188-SM RTX PRO 6000 ([flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#9381](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/9381)).

**No new kernel is needed.** The W4A16 kernel already contains a stripe split-K schedule with a lock-ordered cross-CTA finalize, which the routed-MoE paths use. The dense Trellis host path turned it off in two places:
- `compile_w4a16_gemm` forced `schedule_whole_tiles=True` for `trellis_t256`;
- `run_trellis256_dense` capped the grid at the tile count.

This PR adds an opt-in small-M split-K schedule for dense Trellis plans. It answers the issue's two design questions.

**1. Bit stability: opt-in, off by default.**
- `TrellisQuery` and `query_from_weight` gain `allow_split_k: bool = False`. Default plans keep the whole-tile schedule and today's bits.
- Split-K needs `allow_split_k=True`. `validate_config` rejects a split config otherwise, including through `override`.

The flag is deliberately not named `batch_invariant`. In FlashInfer that name selects the certified mode of `flashinfer.batch_invariant`: properties R1–R4, fingerprints, proved reduction orders and bitwise acceptance tests, defaulting to `False`. Dense Trellis does not meet that standard, with or without this PR.

What dense Trellis does guarantee was measured on RTX PRO 6000; see *Bit-level behaviour* below.
- **Default whole-tile plans.** A row's bits do not depend on the planned M (1–2048, three shapes, including an M whose default tile config differs), on its position, or on its neighbours. A new GPU test pins this.
- **Whole-tile bits depend on `tile_k`** (pre-existing, unchanged here).
  - The kernel folds each K-tile through 2 intra-CTA warp groups at `tile_k=64` and 4 at `tile_k=128`.
  - Every `tile_k=64` config agrees with the default bit for bit; every `tile_k=128` config differs.
  - The existing tuning space admits `tile_k=128`, so an autotuned or overridden plan can differ from the default (4.4e-06–7.6e-05 relative). This is why the configuration-agreement property (R3) does not hold.
- **Split-K plans.**
  - They differ from whole-tile by at most 1.1e-04 relative.
  - A row's bits depend on the slice count. They are identical across M while the count stays the same, and change when the default count changes with M.

**2. Plan-based path: a plan config, chosen at preparation.** A dense Trellis `Plan` is already exact-M (`run` requires `x.shape[0] == query.max_rows`), so each decode M already has its own plan and no launch-time switch is needed.
- `TrellisConfig` gains `split_k_slices: int | None = None`, a tuning knob.
- With `allow_split_k=True`, `default_config` splits K when whole tiles leave at least half the SMs idle.
- Autotune searches `{None, 2, 4, 8, 16}`.

The default slice count was fitted to RTX PRO 6000 sweeps:
- **At most 8 slices.** The finalize is serial per slice, and more than 8 never won.
- **An even split** of the tile's K-tiles, so no slice straggles.
- **At least 512 of K per slice for every two live 16-row blocks.**
- **Within one SM wave.**

Across 24 swept cases (3 shapes × M = 1–128 × 2–16 slices) the default is within 9% of the fastest slice count (geomean 1.008).

Plumbing:
- `compile_w4a16_gemm(schedule_whole_tiles=None)`: `None` keeps the layout default. The flag is recorded in `W4A16GemmCompileResult` and was already part of the kernel cache key.
- `run_trellis256_dense(split_k_slices=None)`: sizes the grid as `mn_tiles × split_k_slices`, capped at the persistent `grid_cap` so every slice is co-resident. It checks that the slice count matches the compiled schedule.
- The trellis_linear tuning contract bumps `query_schema_version` (4→5) and `config_schema_version` (1→2), so cached Trellis tuning entries are re-resolved.
- **No kernel code changes.** The split path reuses the existing finalize:
  - the slice order is fixed, so results are bit-stable run to run and under CUDA-graph replay;
  - the last slice resets the lock word;
  - scratch (`c_tmp`, lock words) is already sized for one partial tile per output tile.

### Scope

- Dense `gemm.trellis_linear` plans (native and P24/P33 pair layouts) on SM120/SM121.
- Opt-in only (`allow_split_k=True`). Default behaviour and bits are unchanged.
- `block_rows == 8` is excluded from split-K: the M8 decode schedule computes one whole tile per CTA by design.
- MoE Trellis paths are untouched.

### Kernel-level performance

Setup:
- **Hardware:** NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120, 188 SMs).
- **Inputs:** K6 MCG Trellis weights (random payload) and FP16 activations.
- **Command:** `python benchmarks/experimental/b12x/benchmark_trellis_dense_split_k.py --sweep`.
- **Timing:** median CUPTI GPU time of the GEMM kernel with a cold L2 every iteration. Both Hadamard rotations are no-ops in the benchmark, so only the Trellis GEMM launches.
- **Arms:** "whole tile" is the default plan. "split" is the `allow_split_k=True` default plan.
- **Error:** relative error is the norm-relative difference of the GEMM output from the whole-tile result.

- The issue's standalone harness reported 117.5 → 41.2 / 80.5 → 35.5 / 46.7 → 26.3 µs at M=4 for the three projections.
- Every split row was bit-identical across repeated runs.

### Bit-level behaviour

Setup: RTX PRO 6000 (SM120), K6 MCG weights, BF16 activations. Every comparison is bitwise (`torch.equal`).

**A. Rows across M.** Each default (whole-tile) plan for M rows against the first M rows of the M=2048 plan.

| K × N | planned M | default configs (block_rows, tile_k, tile_n) | rows bit-equal to the M=2048 plan |

| 6144 × 1024 | 1, 4, 16, 32, 64, 65, 128, 512, 2048 | (64, 64, 256) | all |
| 4096 × 6144 | 1, 4, 16, 32, 64, 65, 128, 512, 2048 | (48, 64, 128); (64, 64, 256) | all |
| 2048 × 4096 | 1, 4, 16, 32, 64, 65, 128, 512, 2048 | (64, 64, 256) | all |

**B. Position and neighbours.** One row at positions 0, 17, 63 of an M=64 plan, among different random neighbours, against the same row run alone: bit-equal at every position.

**C. Configuration agreement.** Every config the tuning contract admits for a whole-tile 6144×1024 plan, against the default config.

**D. Split-K** (`allow_split_k=True` default plans, 6144×1024).

@@ -0,0 +1,283 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Benchmark dense Trellis split-K against the whole-tile schedule.
+
+For each (K, N, M) the script prepares two ``gemm.trellis_linear`` plans on the
+same weight and input:
+
+* ``whole_tile``: the default declaration (one CTA reduces each tile over the full K);
+* ``split_k``: ``allow_split_k=True``, whose default config splits K across
+  CTAs when the whole-tile launch under-fills the GPU.
+
+With ``--sweep`` it also times explicit ``split_k_slices`` overrides at decode
+M, which shows how close the default slice count is to the best one.
+
+Both Hadamard rotations are no-ops over a pre-filled rotated buffer, so each
+timed call launches only the Trellis GEMM kernel. Times are CUPTI kernel
+times with a cold L2 per iteration (``bench_gpu_time``), median in µs.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import statistics
+
+import torch
+
+from b12x.gemm import trellis_linear
+from b12x.gemm.trellis_linear._tuning import TUNING, TrellisConfig
+from b12x.preparation import PreparedCall, PreparationSession
+from b12x.preparation.types import require_prepared
+from flashinfer.testing import bench_gpu_time
+
+# (K, N) projections from the issue's GLM-5.3 EXL3 decode profile.
+DEFAULT_SHAPES = ("6144x1024", "4096x6144", "2048x4096")
+DEFAULT_M = (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 512, 2048)
+SWEEP_SLICES = (2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 12, 16)
+SWEEP_MAX_M = 128
+
+
+def _noop_hadamard(_source, _destination, _left_scale, _right_scale, _scale):
+    """Leave the rotated buffer as filled so only the GEMM kernel launches."""
+
+
+def _time_us(fn, args) -> float:
+    times_ms = bench_gpu_time(
+        fn,
+        enable_cupti=True,
+        cold_l2_cache=True,
+        dry_run_time_ms=args.warmup_ms,
+        repeat_time_ms=args.repeat_ms,
+    )
+    return statistics.median(times_ms) * 1000.0
+
+
+class _Case:
+    def __init__(self, size_k: int, size_n: int, bits: int, device: torch.device):
+        self.size_k = size_k
+        self.size_n = size_n
+        self.device = device
+        generator = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(size_k * 31 + size_n)
+        trellis = torch.randint(
+            -32768,
+            32767,
+            (size_k // 16, size_n // 16, 16 * bits),
+            dtype=torch.int16,
+            device=device,
+            generator=generator,
+        )
+        self.weight = trellis_linear.prepare_weight(
+            trellis,
+            torch.ones(size_k, dtype=torch.float16, device=device),
+            torch.ones(size_n, dtype=torch.float16, device=device),
+            mcg=torch.tensor(0xCBAC1FED, dtype=torch.uint32, device=device),
+            params_dtype=torch.float16,
+        )
+        # packed_gemm_scratch_elements caps c_tmp at SMs * 4 * block_rows * 256
+        # elements; block_rows <= 64 covers every dense Trellis config.
+        sms = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(device).multi_processor_count
+        self.c_tmp = torch.empty(
+            (sms * 4 * 64 * 256,), dtype=torch.float32, device=device
+        )
+
+    def buffers(self, m: int):
+        x = (torch.randn((m, self.size_k), device=self.device) * 1.0e-2).to(
+            torch.float16
+        )
+        rotated = x.clone()
+        gemm_output = torch.empty(
+            (m, self.size_n), dtype=torch.float16, device=self.device
+        )
+        output = torch.empty_like(gemm_output)
+        return x, {
+            "output": output,
+            "gemm_output": gemm_output,
+            "rotated_f16": rotated,
+        }
+
+    def plan(self, x, kwargs, *, allow_split_k: bool, override=None):
+        query = trellis_linear.query_from_weight(
+            self.weight,
+            max_rows=int(x.shape[0]),
+            input_dtype=x.dtype,
+            output_mode="provided",
+            c_tmp_mode="provided",
+            hadamard_128=_noop_hadamard,
+            gemm_output_provided=True,
+            rotated_f16_provided=True,
+            allow_split_k=allow_split_k,
+        )
+        return trellis_linear.plan(
+            query,
+            weight=self.weight,
+            c_tmp=self.c_tmp,
+            hadamard_128=_noop_hadamard,
+            override=override,
+        )
+
+
+def _prepare(session, plan, x, kwargs, name: str):
+    request = plan.request(
+        name=name,
+        prepare_call=lambda state: PreparedCall(run=lambda: state.run(x, **kwargs)),
+    )
+    session.prepare((request,))
+    return require_prepared(plan, "gemm.trellis_linear")
+
+
+def _measure(case: _Case, m: int, args) -> list[dict]:
+    device = case.device
+    x, kwargs = case.buffers(m)
+    rows = []
+    with PreparationSession(
+        device=device, autotune=False, compile_workers=2
+    ) as session:
+        whole_plan = case.plan(x, kwargs, allow_split_k=False)
+        whole_state = _prepare(session, whole_plan, x, kwargs, "whole_tile")
+
+        def run_whole():
+            trellis_linear.run(x, plan=whole_plan, **kwargs)
+
+        run_whole()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize(device)
+        whole = kwargs["gemm_output"].clone()
+        t_whole = _time_us(run_whole, args)
+
+        split_plan = case.plan(x, kwargs, allow_split_k=True)
+        split_state = _prepare(session, split_plan, x, kwargs, "split_k")
+
+        def run_split():
+            trellis_linear.run(x, plan=split_plan, **kwargs)
+
+        run_split()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize(device)
+        split = kwargs["gemm_output"].clone()
+        run_split()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize(device)
+        deterministic = bool(torch.equal(split, kwargs["gemm_output"]))
+        t_split = _time_us(run_split, args)
+        rel_err = float(
+            (split.float() - whole.float()).norm()
+            / whole.float().norm().clamp_min(1e-30)
+        )
+        kernel = whole_state.launch.kernel
+        base = {
+            "K": case.size_k,
+            "N": case.size_n,
+            "M": m,
+            "block_rows": int(kernel.moe_block_size),
+            "tile_k": int(kernel.tile_k),
+            "tile_n": int(kernel.tile_n),
+        }
+        rows.append(
+            {
+                **base,
+                "arm": "default",
+                "split_k_slices": split_state.split_k_slices,
+                "t_whole_tile_us": t_whole,
+                "t_split_k_us": t_split,
+                "speedup": t_whole / t_split,
+                "rel_err_vs_whole_tile": rel_err,
+                "split_k_bit_stable": deterministic,
+            }
+        )
+
+        if not args.sweep or m > SWEEP_MAX_M:
+            return rows
+        for slices in SWEEP_SLICES:
+            # Same tile geometry as the default plans; only the K split varies.
+            override = TrellisConfig(
+                backend="cutedsl",
+                block_rows=base["block_rows"],
+                tile_k=base["tile_k"],
+                tile_n=base["tile_n"],
+                split_k_slices=slices,
+            )
+            try:
+                TUNING.validate_config(split_state.query, override, None)
+            except ValueError:
+                continue
+            plan = case.plan(x, kwargs, allow_split_k=True, override=override)
+            _prepare(session, plan, x, kwargs, f"split_k_{slices}")
+
+            def run_override(plan=plan):
+                trellis_linear.run(x, plan=plan, **kwargs)
+
+            run_override()
+            torch.cuda.synchronize(device)
+            rows.append(
+                {
+                    **base,
+                    "arm": "sweep",
+                    "split_k_slices": slices,
+                    "t_whole_tile_us": t_whole,
+                    "t_split_k_us": _time_us(run_override, args),
+                    "rel_err_vs_whole_tile": float(
+                        (kwargs["gemm_output"].float() - whole.float()).norm()
+                        / whole.float().norm().clamp_min(1e-30)
+                    ),
+                }
+            )
+            rows[-1]["speedup"] = t_whole / rows[-1]["t_split_k_us"]
+    return rows
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
+    parser.add_argument("--shapes", nargs="+", default=list(DEFAULT_SHAPES))
+    parser.add_argument("--m", nargs="+", type=int, default=list(DEFAULT_M))
+    parser.add_argument("--bits", type=int, default=6)
+    parser.add_argument("--sweep", action="store_true")
+    parser.add_argument("--warmup-ms", type=int, default=25)
+    parser.add_argument("--repeat-ms", type=int, default=200)
+    parser.add_argument("--output", help="write all rows as JSON to this path")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
+        raise SystemExit("CUDA is required")
+    device = torch.device("cuda", torch.cuda.current_device())
+    major, minor = torch.cuda.get_device_capability(device)
+    if major != 12:
+        raise SystemExit(f"SM12x required, found sm_{major}{minor}")
+    props = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(device)
+    print(f"device: {props.name} sm_{major}{minor} SMs={props.multi_processor_count}")
+
+    rows = []
+    header = (
+        f"{'K':>5} {'N':>5} {'M':>5} {'arm':>7} {'slices':>6} "
+        f"{'whole us':>9} {'split us':>9} {'speedup':>7} {'rel_err':>8}"
+    )
+    print(header)
+    for shape in args.shapes:
+        size_k, size_n = (int(v) for v in shape.lower().split("x"))
+        case = _Case(size_k, size_n, args.bits, device)
+        for m in args.m:
+            for row in _measure(case, m, args):

# CI workflow using AWS self-hosted runners.
# Runs AOT build tests, GPU unit tests and the CPU-only tests/cpu suite on PRs
# to main, and on main itself on a schedule.
# Uses ci/bash.sh for Docker execution (same as Jenkins).
#
# Permission Control:
# - main: a scheduled full-suite run three times a day (not per merge). Per-merge
#   runs shared one cancel-in-progress group, so each merge cancelled the last:
#   about 90% of them never finished. A scheduled run is never cancelled, runs
#   every lane to completion (no fail-fast), and a failure opens or updates a
#   tracking issue; the next green run closes it.
# - PRs: run when 'run-ci' or the bot's 'run-ci-focused' label is applied.
#   Applying the label is the trigger, so new commits need a new trigger:
#   @flashinfer-bot run.
#
# Instance Purchasing:
# - All runners are on-demand. Spot was removed.
# - A failure here is a real failure, so there is nothing to retry
#   automatically.
# - On-demand capacity is billed for as long as it runs, so the first failure
#   should stop everything else. GitHub only fail-fasts within one matrix, so
#   all tests live in a single matrix built by the setup job. They still start
#   in parallel; the matrix exists purely to make the cancellation global.

name: PR Test

on:
  # Off the 00:00 UTC nightly-release slot; one run per Asia / EU / US workday.
  # Minute 17, not 0: GitHub delays or drops scheduled runs at the top of the hour.
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 4,12,20 * * *'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, labeled, ready_for_review]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      skip_aot:
        description: 'Skip AOT build tests'
        type: boolean
        default: false
      skip_gpu:
        description: 'Skip GPU tests'
        type: boolean
        default: false

concurrency:
  # A label other than run-ci can never start tests, so it gets its own group and
  # does not cancel - otherwise label churn would discard running GPU jobs.
  # Scheduled runs on main get their own group and never cancel each other: at
  # most one runs and one waits, so a slow run delays the next instead of wasting
  # itself.
  group: pr-test-${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' && 'scheduled-' || '' }}${{ github.ref }}${{ (github.event.action == 'labeled' && github.event.label.name != 'run-ci' && github.event.label.name != 'run-ci-focused') && '-noop' || '' }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name != 'schedule' && !(github.event.action == 'labeled' && github.event.label.name != 'run-ci' && github.event.label.name != 'run-ci-focused') }}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  statuses: read # reads the ci/test-scope status published by ci-bot-commands.yml
  actions: read

env:
  EXECUTOR_NUMBER: "0"
  SKIP_CI_PATTERNS: '\.md$|^docs/|^docker/|^licenses/|^LICENSE$|^NOTICE$|^benchmarks/|^\.github/CODEOWNERS$'

jobs:
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Gate - Check if PR is authorized to run CI
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  gate:
    name: Permission Check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      authorized: ${{ steps.check.outputs.authorized }}
    steps:
      - name: Check authorization
        id: check
        env:
          # Read via env, not inlined: a label name is caller-supplied text.
          EVENT_ACTION: ${{ github.event.action }}
          LABEL_NAME: ${{ github.event.label.name }}
        run: |
          # Always allow scheduled runs on main and workflow_dispatch
          if [[ "${{ github.event_name }}" != "pull_request" ]]; then
            echo "authorized=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "Not a PR, authorized"
            exit 0
          fi

          # Authorize on run-ci being applied, not on it being present: presence
          # would re-authorize every later push, which is the auto-trigger this
          # gate removes.
          if [[ "$EVENT_ACTION" == "labeled" && ( "$LABEL_NAME" == "run-ci" || "$LABEL_NAME" == "run-ci-focused" ) ]]; then
            echo "authorized=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "$LABEL_NAME label applied, authorized"
            exit 0
          fi

          echo "authorized=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Not triggered by the run-ci label, skipping CI"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Setup - Read docker tag and check if build should be skipped
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  setup:
    name: Setup
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.authorized == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      docker_tag: ${{ steps.get-tag.outputs.tag }}
      skip_build: ${{ steps.check.outputs.skip }}
      test_matrix: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.matrix }}
      test_count: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.count }}
      # Surfaced so the required check can say a green result was scoped.
      test_scope: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.test_path }}
      h100_disabled: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.h100_disabled }}
      spec_lint_matrix: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.spec_lint_matrix }}
      spec_lint_count: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.spec_lint_count }}
      checkout_sha: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.checkout_sha || github.sha }}
      snapshot_base: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.snapshot_base }}
      snapshot_tree: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.snapshot_tree }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      # Built here rather than written inline in the test job because the
      # `@flashinfer-bot run <paths>` publishes the requested scope as a `ci/test-scope`
      # commit status on this SHA (see ci-bot-commands.yml). Read it verbatim - the
      # comment was parsed once, there, and nothing is re-parsed here.
      #
      # Statuses come back newest-first, so the newest for this context is the last
      # command issued. No status means nobody asked for a scope: run the full suite.
      # Because the status is keyed to the SHA, a scope cannot outlive the commit it was
      # requested for.
      - name: Read requested test scope
        id: scope
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          EVENT_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
          REQUIRE_SNAPSHOT: ${{ github.event.label.name == 'run-ci-focused' }}
        run: |
          # The combined endpoint (/status, not /statuses) returns one entry per
          # context, already the latest. Using it means re-triggering overwrites
          # cleanly without this step deduplicating by hand, and without depending on
          # the raw list's ordering, which is not a documented guarantee.
          STATUSES=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${HEAD_SHA}/status")
          SCOPE=$(jq -r '
              .statuses
              | map(select(.context | test("^ci/test-scope-[0-9]+$")))
              | map({n: (.context | sub("^ci/test-scope-"; "") | tonumber),
                     d: (.description // "")})
              | sort_by(.n) | map(.d) | map(select(. != "")) | join(" ")' <<< "$STATUSES")
          SNAPSHOT=$(jq -r '[.statuses[] | select(.context == "ci/test-snapshot")][0].description // ""' <<< "$STATUSES")
          if [ "${REQUIRE_SNAPSHOT:-false}" = true ] && [ -z "$SNAPSHOT" ]; then
            echo "::error::Automatic test snapshot was cleared or is missing. Issue a new bot run command."
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -n "$SNAPSHOT" ]; then
            if [[ ! "$SNAPSHOT" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}\ [0-9a-f]{40}\ [0-9a-f]{40}\ [0-9a-f]{16}$ ]]; then
              echo "::error::Invalid automatic test snapshot. Issue a new bot run command."
              exit 1
            fi
            read -r SELECTED_BASE SELECTED_MERGE SELECTED_TREE SELECTED_SCOPE <<< "$SNAPSHOT"
            ACTUAL_SCOPE=$(printf '%s' "$SCOPE" | sha256sum | cut -c1-16)
            if [ "$ACTUAL_SCOPE" != "$SELECTED_SCOPE" ]; then
              echo "::error::The automatic scope does not match its snapshot. Issue a new bot run command."
              exit 1
            fi
            # Reconstruct the selected source independently of GitHub's merge ref.
            # No PR scripts, hooks, or submodule contents run during preparation.
            for sha in "$SELECTED_BASE" "$HEAD_SHA"; do
              git cat-file -e "${sha}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null || git fetch --no-tags origin "$sha"
            done
            git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null checkout --detach "$SELECTED_BASE"
            GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 \
              git -c user.name=flashinfer-ci -c user.email=flashinfer-ci@nvidia.com \
              -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c rerere.enabled=false \
              merge --no-ff --no-edit "$HEAD_SHA"
            ACTUAL_TREE=$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')
            if [ "$ACTUAL_TREE" != "$SELECTED_TREE" ]; then
              echo "::error::Merged source differs from AI-selected tree. Issue a new bot run command."
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "Verified AI-selected tree $ACTUAL_TREE (selection $SELECTED_MERGE)"
            echo "checkout_sha=${HEAD_SHA}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "snapshot_base=${SELECTED_BASE}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "snapshot_tree=${SELECTED_TREE}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "checkout_sha=${EVENT_SHA}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          if [ -z "$SCOPE" ]; then
            echo "No requested scope for ${HEAD_SHA}; running the full suite"
          else
            echo "Requested scope: ${SCOPE}"
          fi
          echo "test_path=${SCOPE}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Validate CUDA configuration
        run: python3 ci/validate_cuda_versions.py

      # A shard script that no longer parses fails here, on the PR that changed it,
      # instead of silently un-scheduling later targeted A10G/T4 runs.
      - name: Validate bare-run coverage parse
        run: |
          python3 scripts/infra/pr_checks/targeted_lane_scope.py --coverage-only \
            --scripts scripts/infra/task_jit_run_tests_part{1,2,3,4,5}.sh
          python3 scripts/infra/pr_checks/targeted_lane_scope.py --coverage-only \
            --scripts scripts/infra/task_jit_run_tests_t4.sh

      - name: Get Docker Tag
        id: get-tag
        run: |
          TAG=$(grep 'flashinfer/flashinfer-ci-cu129:' ci/docker-tags.yml | cut -d':' -f2 | tr -d ' ')
          if [ -z "$TAG" ]; then
            echo "::error::Failed to extract Docker tag from ci/docker-tags.yml"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "tag=$TAG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "Docker tag: $TAG"

      - name: Load runtime CUDA matrix
        id: cuda-versions
        run: echo "runtime=$(jq -c '.runtime' ci/cuda-versions.json)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Check Skip Conditions
        id: check
        run: |
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" != "pull_request" ]; then
            echo "skip=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            exit 0
          fi

          # Use PR event SHAs for reliable diff (avoids issues with origin refs)
          BASE_SHA="${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
          HEAD_SHA="${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}"
          CHANGED=$(git diff --name-only "$BASE_SHA...$HEAD_SHA")
          # TODO (yongwww): Add back ^\.github/ before merging to main
          SKIP_PATTERNS="$SKIP_CI_PATTERNS"

          SKIP=true
          while IFS= read -r file; do
            if [ -n "$file" ] && ! echo "$file" | grep -qE "$SKIP_PATTERNS"; then
              SKIP=false
              break
            fi
          done <<< "$CHANGED"

          echo "skip=$SKIP" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          if [ "$SKIP" == "true" ]; then
            echo "::notice::Skipping build - only docs/config files changed"
          fi

      # skip_aot / skip_gpu dispatch inputs have to drop entries before the
      # matrix expands - a job-level `if` cannot see the matrix context, and
      # skipping inside the job would still claim a runner first.
      - name: Build Test Matrix
        id: matrix
        env:
          SKIP_AOT: ${{ github.event.inputs.skip_aot }}
          SKIP_GPU: ${{ github.event.inputs.skip_gpu }}
          RUNTIME_CUDA_MATRIX: ${{ steps.cuda-versions.outputs.runtime }}
          # Targets requested by the triggering `@flashinfer-bot run <paths>` comment,
          # already validated in the step above. Empty for an unparameterised run.
          REQUESTED_TEST_PATH: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.test_path }}
          H100_ON_PRS: 'true'
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
        run: |
          RUN_H100=false
          if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "pull_request" ] && [ "$H100_ON_PRS" != "true" ]; then
            RUN_H100=false
            echo "::notice title=H100 lane disabled on PRs::H100 tests run only in scheduled main runs and manual workflow_dispatch runs until runner capacity is restored" >&2
          fi
          echo "h100_disabled=$([ "$RUN_H100" = "true" ] && echo false || echo true)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # A targeted run on a lane never tests more than that lane's bare run: H100
          # gets the request as-is (its bare run covers tests/); A10G and T4 get it
          # intersected with their shard lists, and a lane left with nothing is skipped.
          # A10G is intersected per shard: each shard whose files overlap the request
          # runs as its own job, so a targeted run keeps the bare run's balancing and
          # -k splits, and shards left with nothing are not scheduled.
          A10G_SCOPES=(); T4_SCOPE=""; H100_SCOPE=""
          if [ "$SKIP_GPU" != "true" ] && [ -n "${REQUESTED_TEST_PATH}" ]; then

              A10G_SCOPES[$shard]=$(python3 scripts/infra/pr_checks/targeted_lane_scope.py \
                --scripts "scripts/infra/task_jit_run_tests_part${shard}.sh" \
                --targets "${REQUESTED_TEST_PATH}")
              echo "A10G shard ${shard} targeted scope: ${A10G_SCOPES[$shard]:-<none: shard not scheduled>}"
            done
            T4_SCOPE=$(python3 scripts/infra/pr_checks/targeted_lane_scope.py \
              --scripts scripts/infra/task_jit_run_tests_t4.sh \
              --targets "${REQUESTED_TEST_PATH}")
            echo "T4 targeted scope:   ${T4_SCOPE:-<none: lane not scheduled>}"
            # tests/cpu belongs to the CPU Unittest lane, which runs on every run.
            # The H100 lane ignores it, so drop it from the H100 scope here: a
            # request naming only tests/cpu then schedules no H100 job instead of
            # one that collects nothing.

                    cuda: $cuda,

            # a CPU test that a scope naming that directory would not select.
            # It needs no GPU and takes about 5 minutes on a CPU runner, and
            # through fail-fast it stops the GPU lanes early when it fails.
            # The GPU lanes leave it out: the H100 lane ignores tests/cpu and
            # the A10G/T4 shard lists name no file under it.

                name: "CPU Unittest",
                kind: "cpu",
                gpu_name: "CPU",
                runner: ["self-hosted", "linux", "x64", "cpu", "on-demand"],
                cuda: "cu129",
                script: "task_run_unit_tests.sh",
                test_path: "tests/cpu",

                  kind: "gpu",
                  gpu_name: "A10G",
                  runner: ["self-hosted", "linux", "x64", "gpu", "sm86", "on-demand"],
                  cuda: "cu129",
                  script: "task_jit_run_tests_part\($shard).sh",
                  timeout: 360

              done

              jq -nc '{
                name: "JIT Unittest (T4)",
                kind: "gpu",
                gpu_name: "T4",
                runner: ["self-hosted", "linux", "x64", "gpu", "sm75", "on-demand"],
                cuda: "cu129",
                script: "task_jit_run_tests_t4.sh",
                timeout: 360
              }'

              if [ "$RUN_H100" = "true" ]; then
                jq -nc '{
                  name: "JIT Unittest (H100)",
                  kind: "h100",
                  gpu_name: "H100",
                  runner: ["self-hosted", "linux", "x64", "gpu", "h100"],
                  cuda: "cu129",
                  script: "task_run_unit_tests.sh",

                  kind: "gpu",
                  gpu_name: "T4",
                  runner: ["self-hosted", "linux", "x64", "gpu", "sm75", "on-demand"],
                  cuda: "cu129",
                  script: "task_run_unit_tests.sh",
                  test_path: $test_path,

                  kind: "h100",
                  gpu_name: "H100",
                  runner: ["self-hosted", "linux", "x64", "gpu", "h100"],
